product_concept: A robust-but-simple US 1099 tax & get-paid toolkit for a specific freelancer sub-niche (e.g. content creators or rideshare/independent contractors): a spreadsheet that gets the SE-tax + quarterly-estimate math right, plus an invoice template and a short setup guide.
core_problem: No withholding, quarterly estimated taxes and Schedule C categories are confusing; generic templates break or don't match the tax regime.
related_problems: don't know how much to set aside for quarterly taxes
spreadsheet formulas break when I edit them
expense categories don't map to Schedule C
desired_outcome: Invoice, track income/expenses, and know what to set aside for taxes without panic at year-end.
core_transformation: From 'no idea what to set aside and formulas that break' → 'know my quarterly number, invoices out, expenses categorised for Schedule C, no tax-season panic'.
product_promise: Know exactly what to set aside every quarter and get paid on time — without an accountant or a broken spreadsheet.
why_this_format: The job is calculation + record-keeping + getting paid, so a spreadsheet/calculator is the native core; a short guide covers the rules; an invoice template closes the get-paid loop. Not an ebook — the value is in the working tool.
product_structure: Auto-calculating spreadsheet (income, expenses, SE tax, quarterly estimate, set-aside %)
Short setup guide (how the rules work, plain-English)
required_sections: How much to set aside (with worked example)
Schedule C categories in plain English
required_worksheets: Deductible-expense checklist by Schedule C line
bonus_assets: Sub-niche category presets (content creator / rideshare / trades)
differentiation: Correct SE-tax + quarterly logic a non-accountant can trust
Formulas that don't break on edit
Tuned to a specific US 1099 sub-niche
Distribution off Etsy (niche community/content), not SEO roulette
price_rationale: Observed: dedicated US trackers sell at $9-25; RunTheCalc does 2.2k sales at ~$17. $15-25 sits in the proven band and above $1 generics without needing subscription justification.
key_customer_language: how much do I set aside for quarterly taxes
I always panic at tax time
key_objections: I can find a free 1099 template
Spreadsheets break when I edit them
I'll just deal with it at tax time
key_buying_motivations: Look professional / get paid on time
evidence_summary: Strong, evidence-backed recurring problem with PROVEN willingness-to-pay ($9-25; RunTheCalc 2.2k sales @ ~$17) and a clear correctness+specificity gap. Main risk is distribution, not demand: incumbents are fragmented but own Etsy search, and free templates compete. Wedge = a specific US 1099 sub-niche + verifiable correctness (SE tax, quarterly estimates, Schedule C) + an off-Etsy distribution angle.
risks_unknowns: Distribution is the hard part (incumbents own Etsy SEO) — UNKNOWN best channel
Tax-logic correctness carries liability; needs careful, disclaimed implementation
Free templates compete; must be visibly better
